synopsis: Full factorial DOE tests every combination of selected factors and levels, allowing main effects and interactions to be established over those tested levels without aliasing [f14101, f7208]. Its run count grows exponentially, so Chapter 9 recommends using it for a small number of important factors and levels and for physical confirmation [f14101, f7210, f7207]. Results cannot establish real-world prevalence unless tested levels are weighted to operational frequency [f7209]. The independent evidence base is NIST methodology; no off-road collision-avoidance study was found, leaving a domain-specific evidence gap [f7212]. Typical tooling includes commercial and open-source statistics packages [f7211].

relations.note: Both state that full factorial run counts grow exponentially.
Testing every combination supports estimating main effects and interactions without aliasing.
Exponential run growth supports limiting the number of factors and levels.
Exponential run growth motivates a small-factor, small-level design.
Limits inference: unaliased tested-level effects do not establish operational prevalence without frequency weighting.
